issues.legal_issue: A state rent-control law may govern cantonment areas after the earlier parliamentary rent-control law for those areas has been repealed and the state law has been extended to them.
material_facts: A parliamentary enactment had provided a separate rent-control regime for cantonments in the state.
A later parliamentary enactment provided that the separate regime would stand repealed when the earlier state rent-control law was extended to the cantonments.
The Central Government issued a notification extending the earlier state rent-control law to the cantonments, after which that law was replaced by a new state rent-control enactment.
A subsequent notification extended the new state enactment to the cantonments. The challenged rent-release order was made under that enactment.
issues.conclusion: The earlier parliamentary rent-control regime ceased to apply when the state law was extended, and the state rent-control enactment could apply to the cantonments; the separate earlier regime did not prevent its application.
issues.legal_principle: The repeal enactment expressly made the cessation of the earlier parliamentary regime conditional on extension of the state rent-control law under section 3 of the Cantonments (Extension of Rent Control Laws) Act, 1957. The Court held that the condition was met by the notification extending the earlier state law. The repeal enactment merely removed the obstacle to that extension; it did not incorporate the earlier state law into itself. The Court also relied on the retrospective operation given to the 1957 Act and rejected the contention that it excluded the state merely because a separate parliamentary law had once applied there.

rule.if: cantonment_rent_control_proceeding and (separate_parliamentary_rent_regime_applied or state_rent_law_extended_to_cantonment) and separate_regime_terminated_on_extension

predicates.cantonment_rent_control_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the application of rent-control law to premises in a cantonment.
predicates.separate_parliamentary_rent_regime_appli: A parliamentary rent-control regime had applied to the cantonment before the state rent-control law was extended there.
predicates.state_rent_law_extended_to_cantonment: The central authority extended the state rent-control law to the cantonment.
predicates.separate_regime_terminated_on_extension: A parliamentary enactment provided that the separate rent-control regime would cease when the state rent-control law was extended.

issues.definition: When a cantonment rent-control proceeding involves an extended state rent law and the separate parliamentary regime was made to end upon that extension, the state rent-control law applies to the cantonment.

issues.legal_issue: The power to extend state rent-control legislation to cantonments may be exercised again when the state legislation is replaced or amended.
material_facts: The Central Government first issued a notification extending the earlier state rent-control law to the cantonments.
The state later replaced that law with a new rent-control enactment, and the Central Government issued a further notification extending the new enactment.
The Central Government later issued another notification extending the state enactment as amended, superseding the earlier notification.
The statutory framework had been amended to permit extension of state legislation as in force in the state, rather than only as it stood on the date of a notification.
issues.conclusion: The power was not exhausted by the first notification. The later notifications were valid, and the amended state rent-control provisions could be extended to the cantonments.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the Cantonments (Extension of Rent Control Laws) Act, 1957, as amended by the Cantonments (Extension of Rent Control Laws) Amendment Act, 1972, permits notifications to be issued as occasion arises so that cantonments continue to have the same rent-control law as the rest of the state. Sections 14 and 21 of the General Clauses Act, 1897, support the continued exercise of the notification power. The Court applied Gurcharan Singh v. V. K. Kaushal and distinguished Lachmi Narain v. Union: the later notifications responded to replacement or amendment of the state law rather than merely revising, without such a change, the terms of an earlier extension.

rule.if: cantonment_rent_control_proceeding and prior_extension_notification_issued and (state_rent_law_replaced or state_rent_law_amended) and later_extension_notification_issued

predicates.cantonment_rent_control_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the extension or application of rent-control law to a cantonment.
predicates.prior_extension_notification_issued: The central authority had previously extended a state rent-control law to the cantonment.
predicates.state_rent_law_replaced: The state rent-control law previously extended to the cantonment was later replaced by another state rent-control law.
predicates.state_rent_law_amended: The state rent-control law previously extended to the cantonment was later amended in the state.
predicates.later_extension_notification_issued: The central authority issued a further notification after the state law had been replaced or amended.

issues.definition: A later extension notification is valid in a cantonment rent-control proceeding when an earlier extension exists, the state law has since been replaced or amended, and a further notification follows.

issues.legal_issue: Parliament does not impermissibly delegate its legislative function by authorising the extension of state rent-control laws to cantonments, including future amendments, subject to limited modifications.
material_facts: Parliament chose as a policy that cantonment residents should generally be governed by the same rent-control legislation as residents in the rest of the state.
The extension mechanism applied legislation already in force in the state and permitted restrictions or modifications to adapt it to cantonment conditions.
The delegated power did not permit changes to the essential character, material provisions, or legislative policy of the state law.
The challenge alleged that Parliament had delegated decisions about future state laws and modifications without applying its own mind to their details.
issues.conclusion: The delegation was valid and did not amount to an abdication of Parliament’s legislative function; future amendments to the state rent-control law could also be extended to cantonments.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied section 3 of the Cantonments (Extension of Rent Control Laws) Act, 1957, as amended, and held that the power to make restrictions and modifications is confined to peripheral changes needed to adapt an enactment, not changes to its essential character or policy. It relied on the Delhi Laws Act case and Raj Narain Singh v. Chairman, Patna Administration Committee for the limits on delegated legislation; distinguished B. Shama Rao v. Union Territory of Pondicherry, where there was a total surrender of legislative responsibility; and relied on Gwalior Rayon’s case and Sita Ram Bishambher Dayal v. State of U.P. in recognising the validity of delegation within a defined legislative policy. It also applied the principle that adopting future laws or amendments is not invalid where the legislature has made the governing policy clear and the delegate cannot alter the law’s essential features.

predicates.delegation_validity_challenged: A party challenges the validity of a legislative delegation used to extend rent-control law to cantonments.
predicates.parliament_set_statewide_parity_policy: The legislature chose the policy that cantonments should generally follow the same rent-control law as other areas of the state.
predicates.delegated_power_limited_to_extending_sta: The delegate's authority is to extend rent-control legislation already in force in the state to cantonments.
predicates.modifications_cannot_change_essential_po: The delegate cannot use adaptations or modifications to change the essential character or policy of the extended law.

issues.definition: A delegation is valid when the legislature chooses statewide parity, the delegate extends the state rent law, and any permitted adaptations cannot alter that law’s essential policy.

issues.legal_issue: An order made under the state rent-control law in force at the time may be preserved as an order under the later-extended amended law, even if the amendment had not yet been expressly extended to the cantonment when the order was made.
material_facts: The notification extending the new state enactment to cantonments limited the extension to that enactment as it stood on the notification date.
The state later amended the enactment, including provisions governing the prescribed authority, and the amendments were extended to cantonments by a later notification.
Before that later notification, a rent-control application was transferred to and decided by an authority appointed under the state law as then in force.
The later extension took effect before the appellate proceedings were concluded.
issues.conclusion: Although the earlier notification did not itself extend later amendments, the order was preserved and deemed to have been made under the corresponding provisions of the amended rent-control law extended to the cantonment.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(4) of the Cantonments (Extension of Rent Control Laws) Act, 1957, as amended, deems qualifying orders made under the state law in force before extension to have been made under the corresponding provisions of the extended rent-control law. The Court applied Jai Singh Jairam Tyagi v. Mamanchand Ratilal Agarwal, which held that this saving provision applies independently of whether the extension is retrospective, and S. P. Jain v. Krishna Mohan Gupta, which applied the saving rule to proceedings under the amended state rent law. The Court separately held that the earlier notification’s express limitation to the law as it stood on its date could not be ignored.

rule.if: cantonment_rent_control_proceeding and prior_order_made_under_state_law and authority_valid_under_state_law and later_extension_covers_corresponding_law

predicates.cantonment_rent_control_proceeding: The proceeding concerns a rent-control order relating to premises in a cantonment.
predicates.prior_order_made_under_state_law: An order was made under the rent-control law then in force in the state before that law or its relevant amendment was extended to the cantonment.
predicates.authority_valid_under_state_law: The authority that made the order was appointed and empowered under the state law then in force.
predicates.later_extension_covers_corresponding_law: A later extension brings the corresponding state rent-control law or amendment within the law applicable to the cantonment.

issues.definition: A prior order is saved under the extended law when it was made in a cantonment rent-control proceeding by an authority valid under the then-current state law and a later extension covers the corresponding law.
